# Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users

Day 3, 14:20 · Nik Vujic, a community speaker · lightning · coverage: transcript, one-slide

Nik Vujic (Founder, Get Stuff Digital) on Search Console data through BigQuery and an LLM agent, named from his self-introduction, which matches the official speaker list; then a community speaker who was not named, on AI visibility and brand familiarity. Other talks of this block were not captured.

- **[Stage]** Nik Vujic said his agency uses the Search Console data fed to an LLM in five use cases, the first being cross-comparing and following up different articles.
  <br><sub>`D3-C482` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (Nik Vujic)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Nik Vujic said that after a page is published, the queries it appears for are the first thing to show up in Search Console, while clicks and impressions come much later.
  <br><sub>`D3-C483` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (Nik Vujic) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Analysis]** A query reaches Search Console's Performance report only through an impression, so queries cannot come before impressions; what rises first after a publish or refresh is the number of queries with a few impressions each, before total impressions and clicks grow noticeably.
  <br><sub>`D3-C484` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users</sub>

- **[Stage]** To report content refreshes on large sites, Nik Vujic's agency compares date ranges and has an LLM give the exact number of queries the content improved on, then reports that number to the client.
  <br><sub>`D3-C485` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (Nik Vujic)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Nik Vujic said Google loves fresh, quality content, as a reason for large sites to refresh their content.
  <br><sub>`D3-C486` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (Nik Vujic) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's ranking systems guide describes 'query deserves freshness' systems that show fresher content where it would be expected, which is narrower than a general preference for fresh content; refresh pages whose queries expect current information, and judge other refreshes by quality.

  <br><sub>`D3-C498` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · is the documentation · [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) · Extends [D3-C438](D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) · Used by `DEV-MON-07`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Search Console's branded queries filter works only for top-level properties, not URL-path or subdomain properties, and only for sites with enough queries and impressions; Google made it available to all eligible sites on 11 March 2026.
  <br><sub>`D3-C499` · Search Central blog (20 November 2025, updated 11 March 2026) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · is the documentation · [Introducing the branded queries filter in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/11/search-console-branded-filter) · Used by the glossary term *Branded queries filter*</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Because Google says anonymized queries are left out whenever a filter is applied, branded plus non-branded exports should not be expected to add up to the unfiltered chart totals; tell an LLM that sums filtered exports that the gap is expected, not missing data.
  <br><sub>`D3-C500` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · [A deep dive into Search Console performance data filtering and limits](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2022/10/performance-data-deep-dive)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Before feeding a branded versus non-branded split to an LLM, spot-check a sample of queries in each group, since Google's AI-assisted classification can misidentify queries; on URL-path or subdomain properties, where the filter is unavailable, a regex query filter is the fallback.
  <br><sub>`D3-C501` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · [Introducing the branded queries filter in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/11/search-console-branded-filter) · Extends [D3-C435](D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Looker Studio lifts Search Console's 1,000-row interface limit but keeps the connector's cap of 50,000 rows per day per site per search type; only the bulk export to BigQuery is free of the daily row limit, so large sites that need every non-anonymized query should use it.

- **[Docs]** A May 2025 Search Central blog post advised site owners to look at the overall value of visits from Search rather than focusing too much on clicks, using indicators of conversion such as sales, sign-ups, a more engaged audience or information lookups about the business.
  <br><sub>`D3-C536` · Search Central blog (21 May 2025) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · is the documentation · [Top ways to ensure your content performs well in Google's AI experiences on Search](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/05/succeeding-in-ai-search) · Extends [D1-C057](D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** For the brand in a community speaker's controlled test, organic sessions in GA4 roughly halved while direct sessions stayed fairly stable (an uncertain reading; a change of about 2% was mentioned, direction unclear in the recording).
  <br><sub>`D3-C537` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker advised comparing the relative performance of channels and choosing new metrics to report, rather than judging SEO on organic sessions alone.
  <br><sub>`D3-C538` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A fully controlled test of AI visibility was possible for one brand only because it ran no other marketing activity, and is not viable for most brands, a community speaker said.
  <br><sub>`D3-C539` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker recommended picking areas of a business where testing is possible and measuring how AI visibility affects conversion rates and revenue there.
  <br><sub>`D3-C540` · Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** The community speaker's figures (paid search click-through rate up 36%, organic sessions halved, a record month) come from one unpublished test of one unnamed brand with no stated period or baseline; use them as an illustration, not as a benchmark.
  <br><sub>`D3-C541` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's own line on Day 1 was to measure success by metrics that matter to the business, and its Generative AI performance report shows impressions but no clicks; together with the community talk this argues for a report that puts organic next to direct, branded paid search, conversions and revenue.
  <br><sub>`D3-C542` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · Extends [D1-C057](D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Extends [D1-C124](D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For a site's own test of AI visibility, write down the period, the baseline and every other marketing change before starting, and compare a test area with a similar control area; paid click-through rate and direct and branded traffic are the signals the community speaker watched.
  <br><sub>`D3-C543` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users</sub>

- **[Analysis]** The two studies cited on stage are third-party and narrow (Similarweb, 2026: ChatGPT only, US desktop, three industries; Red C, 2018: eye-tracking on shopping-type searches), so quote them with that scope; Similarweb found that 55.9% of the resulting site traffic came from branded searches, the step after an AI recommendation in the speaker's customer journey.
  <br><sub>`D3-C544` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Lightning session L: Understanding SERPs and your users · [AI-Recommended Brands Saw 2.5x More Site Visits: Similarweb](https://www.searchenginejournal.com/ai-recommended-brands-saw-2-5x-more-site-visits-similarweb/580241/), [82% of searchers choose a familiar brand for the first click [study]](https://econsultancy.com/82-percent-searchers-choose-familiar-brand-search/)</sub>
